item.title: [翻译] Dwarkesh Patel: AI重大问题博客征文奖
item.description:
标签: #AI发展 #AI商业化 #AI治理 #博客奖金

摘要: 作者宣布设立2万美元博客征文奖，征集关于AI发展速度、基础模型盈利、巨额慈善资金部署及非AI国家应对策略等重大问题的千字短文；此举的真正目的是寻找一位研究合作者，与其共同深入探索这些关乎经济、政策与超级智能治理的关键议题。

原标题: Blog prize for the big questions about AI

Blog prize for the big questions about AI

There has never been a time where excellent intellectual output on the right question has been more valuable or more urgent. Compelling answers about the big questions about AI can inform the most important economic and foreign policy decisions that will ever be made, the deployment of (at least)hundreds of billionsof philanthropic dollars, and the training and governance of superintelligences.

当下，针对正确问题的卓越思想产出从未如此宝贵且紧迫。关于 AI 宏大问题（big questions）的有力回答，能够为有史以来最重要的经济与外交政策决策提供参考，能够影响（至少）数千亿慈善资金的部署，并关乎超级智能（superintelligences）的训练与治理。

I’m announcing a $20,000 blog prize in order to find people who will excel at researching and thinking through these problems. The not-so-secret point of this whole contest is so that I can hire a research collaborator to think through questions like this hand in hand with me. See more at the end.

我宣布设立一笔2 万美元博客奖金（$20,000 blog prize），以寻找那些擅长研究并深入思考这些问题的人才。这场竞赛的“公开秘密”在于，我希望借此聘请一位研究合作者（research collaborator），与我携手共同探讨这类问题。更多详情见文末。

Pick a question below, and spend no more than 1,000 words answering it. 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place will get $10,000, $6,000, and $4,000 respectively. I’ll publish the winning entry (and potentially the runner ups) on my blog. Please submit by May 10th, 11:59 PM PST.

从下方选择一个问题，用不超过 1000 字的篇幅作答。第一名、第二名和第三名（1st, 2nd, and 3rd place）将分别获得 1 万美元、6000 美元和 4000 美元。我会将获奖文章（以及可能的入围作品）发布在我的博客上。请在太平洋标准时间（PST）5 月 10 日晚 11:59 前提交。

Questions - choose one

  • A couple years ago, there was this idea that AI progress might slow down as we make further progress into the RL regime. 1. Because as horizon lengths increase, the AI needs to do many days’ worth of work before we can even see if it did it right, so if we’re still in a naive policy gradient world, the reward signal / FLOP goes down, and 2. We’d crossed through many OOMs of RL compute from GPT 4 to o1 to o3, and it would not be feasible to replicate that many OOMs increase in compute immediately again. But AI progress seems to have been fast nonetheless - even potentially speeding up if rumors about Spud or Mythos are to be believed. What gives? What did that previous intuition pump that motivated longer timelines miss?

几年前，人们曾有一种观点：随着我们在强化学习阶段（RL regime）中不断深入，AI 的进展可能会放缓。理由有二：1. 随着视界长度（horizon lengths）增加，AI 需要完成多日工作量后，我们才能判断其是否正确完成，因此如果我们仍处于朴素的策略梯度（policy gradient）时代，奖励信号 /浮点运算次数（FLOP）会下降；2. 从 GPT-4 到 o1 再到 o3，我们已经跨越了多个数量级（OOMs, Orders of Magnitude）的 RL 计算量，短期内再次复制如此多数量级的算力增长是不可行的。但尽管如此，AI 的进步似乎依然迅速——如果关于 Spud 或 Mythos 的传闻属实，甚至可能还在加速。这是怎么回事？当初支撑更长 timelines 预期的那个直觉泵（intuition pump）遗漏了什么？

  • What’s the most plausible story where foundation model companies actually start making money? If you consider each individual model as a company, then its profitsmaybe able to pay back the training cost. But of course, if you don’t train a bigger, more expensive model immediately, then you stop making money after 3 months. So when does the profit start? Maybe at some point scaling will plateau, butif progress at the frontierhas slowed down, then the combination of distillation and low switching costs (cloud margins result from high switching costs) makes it really easy for open source to catch up to the labs, eating into their margins. So how do the labs actually start making money?

基础模型公司真正开始盈利的最可信路径是什么？如果你把每一个单独的模型视为一家公司，那么它的利润或许能够回本。但当然，如果你不立即训练一个更大、更昂贵的模型，3 个月后你就会停止盈利。那么利润从何时开始？也许在某个时刻，规模扩展（scaling）会触及平台期，但如果前沿进展放缓，那么知识蒸馏（distillation）与低切换成本（云服务商的利润正来自于高切换成本）的结合，会让开源模型轻易追上实验室的水平，侵蚀它们的利润。那么这些实验室究竟如何才能真正赚钱？

  • With OpenAI’s new raise at an $852B valuation, OpenAI Foundation’s stake isnow worth $180B. Anthropic’scofounders have pledged to donate 80%of their wealth. Nobody seems to have a concrete idea of how to deploy 100s of billions (soon trillions) of wealth productively to “make AI go well”. If you were in charge of the OpenAI Foundation right now, what exactly would you do? And when? It’s not enough to identify a cause you think is important, because that doesn’t answer the fundamental problem ofhow you convert money to impact. Identify the concrete strategy you recommend pursuing.

随着 OpenAI 以 8520 亿美元估值完成新一轮融资，OpenAI 基金会（OpenAI Foundation）持有的股份现价值 1800 亿美元。Anthropic 的联合创始人已承诺捐赠其 80% 的财富。目前似乎没有人对如何 productive 地部署数千亿（很快将是数万亿）财富以“让 AI 健康发展”有具体思路。如果你现在掌管 OpenAI 基金会，你具体会做什么？何时做？仅仅指出你认为重要的事业是不够的，因为这并没有回答如何将资金转化为实际影响力的根本问题。请明确你建议采取的具体策略。

  • What should countries which are not currently in the AI production chain (semis, energy, frontier models, robotics) do in order to not get totally sidestepped by transformative AI? If you’re the leader of India or Nigeria, what do you do right now?

那些目前尚未处于 AI 生产链（半导体、能源、前沿模型、机器人）中的国家，应该采取什么措施，才能不被变革性人工智能（transformative AI）完全绕过或边缘化？如果你是 印度（India）或 尼日利亚（Nigeria）的领导人，你现在会怎么做？

Rules and tips

  • Please don’t let a lack of domain expertise dissuade you from entering. I’m looking for someone who can ramp up fast on unfamiliar topics and think clearly.

请不要因缺乏领域专业知识而却步。我需要的是能够快速熟悉陌生话题并保持清晰思考的人。

  • Each entrant may submit only once.

每位参赛者只能提交一次。

  • You are still eligible for this essay competition even if you’re not interested in the researcher role. Nor does winning this competition guarantee that you will be offered the role.

即使你对研究员职位不感兴趣，你仍然有资格参加本次征文竞赛。此外，赢得竞赛并不保证你会获得该职位。

  • You’re welcome to use LLMs to help you research, but I specifically picked these questions because I’ve found LLM answers to them unsatisfying. On these kinds of ambiguous questions, LLMs are too all over the place. For example, they’ll identify 5 plausible answers but not have the context and taste to identify the crucial factor and iron out its implications.

欢迎使用大语言模型（LLMs）辅助研究，但我专门挑选这些问题，正是因为我发现 LLM 给出的答案并不令人满意。在这类模棱两可的问题上，LLM 的回答往往过于分散。例如，它们可能会列出 5 个看似合理的答案，但却缺乏背景和判断力去识别关键因素并梳理其影响。

  • You only have 1000 words - make them count. People have the habit ofspending the first paragraphs clearing their throat- avoid that.

你只有 1000 字——务必物尽其用。人们常常习惯在开头几段铺垫寒暄，请避免这种做法。

Why am I hiring for a researcher?

I want my podcast/blog to move from just asking questions about AI to actually helping answer them. But there are too many important questions, and I need a collaborator to build up context on them all, to explore dozens of fractal sub-questions, to consider the rebuttals and syntheses, and to sharpen each others thinking.

我希望自己的播客/博客能从仅仅提出 AI 问题，转向真正帮助回答问题。但重要的问题太多了，我需要一个合作者来建立全局背景知识，探索数十个分形子问题（fractal sub-questions），思考各种反驳与综合，并相互磨砺思维。

The questions I want us to explore are very broad while at the same time requiring deep technical analysis across many domains to actually answer.

我们想要探索的问题非常宽泛，同时又需要跨多个领域进行深入的技术分析才能真正回答。

Why am I hiring this way?

Well, I could just put out a job ad for a researcher, but I’ll get 1,000 different resumes, and I’ll have no clue based on that information whether the applicant would be any good at synthesizing lots of technical arguments and information. So I thought, let’s just list out some questions where I genuinely don’t know the answer and would be keen to get some insight.

好吧，我也可以直接发布一份研究员招聘广告，但我会收到 1000 份不同的简历，而我无法从中判断应聘者是否擅长综合大量技术论点与信息。于是我想，不如直接列出一些我自己也真心不知道答案、并且渴望获得见解的问题。

What this role looks like

  • Ideally in person in San Francisco, but potentially open to remote.

理想情况下在旧金山线下工作，但也可考虑远程。

  • Will pay competitively

薪酬具有竞争力。

Submit here

If you have questions or comments, I’m hello@dwarkeshpatel.com.

如有问题或评论，请发邮件至 hello@dwarkeshpatel.com。

item.title: [翻译] Simon Willison: 服务“为你推荐”信息流
item.description:
标签: #推荐系统 #系统架构 #低成本

摘要: 本文介绍了Bluesky"For You"推荐流的极简架构：开发者仅凭一台客厅游戏PC（单Go进程+SQLite）和一台月费7美元的VPS，以每月30美元的成本为数万用户提供服务，并估计该系统足以支撑百万日活用户。

原标题: Serving the For You feed

Serving the For You feed

为你推荐（For You）信息流的服务架构

spacecowboy runs theFor You Feed, used by around 72,000 people. This guest post on the AT Protocol blog explains how it works.

spacecowboy 运营着 For You Feed（为你推荐信息流），服务于约 72,000 名用户。这篇发布在 AT Protocol（AT 协议）博客上的客座文章解释了它的工作原理。

The architecture isfascinating. The feed is served by a single Go process using SQLite on a "gaming" PC in spacecowboy's living room - 16 cores, 96GB of RAM and 4TB of attached NVMe storage.

其架构设计令人着迷。该信息流由一台在 spacecowboy 客厅“游戏”PC 上运行的单 Go 语言进程通过 SQLite 提供服务——这台电脑配备 16 核 CPU、96GB 内存以及 4TB 外接 NVMe 存储。

Recommendations are based on likes: what else are the people who like the same things as you liking on the platform?

Recommendations（推荐内容）基于 likes（点赞）：与你喜好相似的人还在平台上点赞了哪些内容？

That Go server consumes the Bluesky firehose and stores the relevant details in SQLite, keeping the last 90 days of relevant data, which currently uses around 419GB of SQLite storage.

这台 Go server（Go 服务器）消费 Bluesky 的 firehose（实时全量数据流），并将相关详情存入 SQLite，仅保留最近 90 天的相关数据，目前约占用了约 419GB 的 SQLite 存储空间。

Public internet traffic is handled by a $7/month VPS on OVH, which talks to the living room server via Tailscale.

公网流量由一台每月 7 美元的 VPS（虚拟专用服务器，托管于 OVH）处理，它通过 Tailscale 与客厅中的服务器通信。

Total cost is now $30/month: $20 in electricity, $7 in VPS and $3 for the two domain names. spacecowboy estimates that the existing system could handle all ~1 million daily active Bluesky users if they were to switch to the cheapest algorithm they have found to work.

目前的总成本为每月 30 美元：20 美元电费、7 美元 VPS 费用以及 3 美元的两个域名费用。spacecowboy 估计，如果切换到他们发现的成本最低的可用 algorithm（算法），现有系统足以承载全部约 100 万 Bluesky 日活跃用户。

Tags: go, scaling, sqlite, software-architecture, tailscale, bluesky

item.title: [翻译] Simon Willison: Claude Code 质量报告更新
item.description:
标签: #Claude #代码智能体 #质量报告 #Bug

摘要: Anthropic解释近期Claude Code的质量问题并非模型本身所致，而是由其工程框架中的三个独立bug引起，其中一个会话记忆清除机制的缺陷导致AI在长会话中显得健忘和重复。作者借此提醒，构建智能体系统时需格外警惕这类复杂的工程层问题，而非仅关注模型本身的非确定性。

原标题: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports

An update on recent Claude Code quality reports

The models themselves were not to blame, but three separate issues in the Claude Code harness caused complex but material problems which directly affected users.

模型本身并非罪魁祸首，但 Claude Code 的 harness（运行框架）中存在三个独立的问题，引发了复杂但实质性的故障，直接影响了用户体验。

Anthropic's postmortem describes these in detail. This one in particular stood out to me:

Anthropic 发布的事后分析报告（postmortem）详细描述了这些问题。其中有一点尤其引起了我的注意：

On March 26, we shipped a change to clear Claude's older thinking from sessions that had been idle for over an hour, to reduce latency when users resumed those sessions. A bug caused this to keep happening every turn for the rest of the session instead of just once, which made Claude seem forgetful and repetitive.

3 月 26 日，我们发布了一项变更，用于清除闲置超过一小时的会话中 Claude 先前的思考内容，以降低用户恢复会话时的延迟（latency）。但一个 bug 导致该操作在会话后续的每一轮交互中持续触发，而非仅执行一次，这使得 Claude 表现得健忘且重复。

On March 26, we shipped a change to clear Claude's older thinking from sessions that had been idle for over an hour, to reduce latency when users resumed those sessions. A bug caused this to keep happening every turn for the rest of the session instead of just once, which made Claude seem forgetful and repetitive.

3 月 26 日，我们发布了一项变更，用于清除闲置（idle）超过一小时的会话中 Claude 先前的思考内容，以降低用户恢复会话时的延迟。但一个 bug 导致该操作在会话后续的每一轮交互中持续触发，而非仅执行一次，这使得 Claude 表现得健忘且重复（repetitive）。

Ifrequentlyhave Claude Code sessions which I leave for an hour (or often a day or longer) before returning to them. Right now I have 11 of those (according tops aux | grep 'claude ') and that's after closing down dozens more the other day.

我经常会让 Claude Code 会话闲置一小时（甚至常常是一天或更久）后才返回继续工作。目前我正开着 11 个这样的会话（根据 tops aux | grep 'claude ' 的输出），而这还是在我前几天关闭了几十个之后的数量。

I estimate I spend more time prompting in these "stale" sessions than sessions that I've recently started!

我估计自己在这些"陈旧"（stale）会话中花费的 prompting（提示词输入）时间，比在近期新开会话中还要多！

If you're building agentic systems it's worth reading this article in detail - the kinds of bugs that affect harnesses are deeply complicated, even if you put aside the inherent non-deterministic nature of the models themselves.

如果你正在构建 agentic systems（智能体系统），这篇文章值得一读——影响 harness 的 bug 类型极其复杂，即使抛开模型本身固有的 非确定性（non-deterministic）本质不谈。

ViaHacker News

item.title: [翻译] Simon Willison: Honker：为 SQLite 带来队列与流处理的扩展
item.description:
标签: #SQLite #消息队列 #数据库

摘要: Honker 是一款专为 SQLite 设计的扩展，它通过简洁的 Python API 和 20 余种自定义 SQL 函数，实现了类 Kafka 的队列与持久化流功能。其核心在于内置事务性发件箱模式，确保消息仅在事务成功提交后才入队，并支持以轮询 WAL 文件的方式实现近实时的消息消费。

原标题: russellromney/honker

russellromney/honker

The design of this looks very solid. It lets you write Python code for queues that looks like this: 
import honker

db = honker.open("app.db")
emails = db.queue("emails")
emails.enqueue({"to": "alice@example.com"})

# Consume (in a worker process)
async for job in emails.claim("worker-1"):
    send(job.payload)
    job.ack()

这个项目的设计看起来非常扎实。它允许你编写用于 queues（队列）的 Python 代码，形式如下：

And Kafka-style durable streams like this: 
stream = db.stream("user-events")

with db.transaction() as tx:
    tx.execute("UPDATE users SET name=? WHERE id=?", [name, uid])
    stream.publish({"user_id": uid, "change": "name"}, tx=tx)

async for event in stream.subscribe(consumer="dashboard"):
    await push_to_browser(event)

以及如下所示的 Kafka-style（Kafka 风格）durable streams（持久化流）：

It also adds 20+ custom SQL functions including these two: 
SELECT notify('orders', '{"id": 42}');
SELECT honker_stream_read_since('orders', 0, 1000);

它还增加了 20 多个自定义的 SQL functions（SQL 函数），其中包括以下两个：

The extension requires WAL mode, and workers can poll the .db-wal file with a stat call every 1ms to get as close to real-time as possible without the expense of running a full SQL query.

该扩展需要 WAL mode（预写日志模式），并且 workers（工作进程）可以每 1 毫秒通过 stat 调用轮询 .db-wal 文件，从而在不运行完整 SQL query（SQL 查询）开销的前提下，尽可能接近 real-time（实时）。

honker implements the transactional outbox pattern, which ensures items are only queued if a transaction successfully commits. My favorite explanation of that pattern remains Transactionally Staged Job Drains in Postgres by Brandur Leach. It's great to see a new implementation of that pattern for SQLite.

honker 实现了 transactional outbox pattern（事务性发件箱模式），确保仅当事务成功提交时，条目才会被入队。关于该模式，我最喜欢的解释仍然是 Brandur Leach 写的《Transactionally Staged Job Drains in Postgres》。很高兴看到针对 SQLite 的这一模式有了新实现。

item.title: [翻译] Simon Willison: 毫秒转换器
item.description:
标签: #时间换算 #单位转换 #实用工具

摘要: 由于LLMreports默认以毫秒显示提示词耗时，手动换算为秒和分钟颇为繁琐，作者因此开发了一款毫秒转换工具来简化这一过程。

原标题: Millisecond Converter

Millisecond Converter

LLMreports reports prompt durations in milliseconds and I got fed up of having to think about how to convert those to seconds and minutes.

LLMreports 以 milliseconds（毫秒）为单位报告 prompt（提示词）的持续时间，我受够了每次都要动脑筋把它们换算成秒和分钟。

🔗 阅读原文
